name: sales
description: B2B sales memory: deals, accounts, contacts and reps from the CRM, plus what calls, emails and notes say about them (stakeholders, commitments, objections, competitors, qualification).

deal.description: An opportunity. Ids are deal:<crm id>.

stage.description: The org's own pipeline stages (open enum).

current_tool.description: a tool they use today relevant to the deal, including in-house tools and home-built attempts that failed; keep the key specifics

account.description: A company, or a household in wealth management. Ids are account:<id>.

current_process.description: one step of how they onboard, train or coach reps today, e.g. 'two weeks shadowing a senior rep before taking calls'

product_line.description: a line of business, including the business mix ('mostly commercial accounts') and lines they no longer sell

sales_language.description: a language their reps sell in

contact.description: A person at an account. Ids are contact:<id>.

company.description: The company name on the CRM record, which may name a company that has no account.

stakeholder.description: A contact's part in one deal: an edge with properties. Ids are stakeholder:<deal id>:<contact id>.

rep.description: A seller on our side. Ids are rep:<user id>.

meeting.description: A call or meeting. Ids are meeting:<id>.

commitment.description: Something someone said they would do. Ids are commitment:<id>.

task.description: A to-do in AmpUp or the CRM; its name is the subject. Ids are task:<id>.

status.description: open, completed, dismissed, expired and the like (open enum).

source.description: Where the task came from, such as AmpUp or hubspot.

objection.description: A concern a buyer raised. Ids are objection:<id>.

category.description: The org's own objection categories (open enum).

raised_in.description: The meetings it came up in, so counts per meeting work.

competitor.description: Another vendor in the deal. Ids are competitor:<slug>.

coaching_signal.description: An observation about a rep's selling. Ids are coaching_signal:<id>.

pipeline_by_stage.title: Open pipeline by stage
pipeline_by_stage.description: Open deals per stage, with their total amount.

objections_by_deal_stage.title: Objections by deal stage
objections_by_deal_stage.description: Objections per stage of the deal they are about.

open_commitments_by_owner.title: Open commitments by owner
open_commitments_by_owner.description: Open or stale commitments per owner.

guidance: Deals won in a period: count by close_date, which the CRM sets when a deal is won. Deals lost in a period: a lost deal's close_date often keeps its old expected date, so count by when its status changed to lost (find changes with type deal, select ["status"] and that window). When close_date and the status change disagree, say which you counted.

A stakeholder's CRM role is often missing or stale. For who decides, the champion or a blocker, also read passages about the deal (deal context, qualification reviews, calls) and say where they disagree with the CRM.
Tasks are records, not passages: find them with type task, for example where {"rel": "deal", "to": {"id": "deal:<id>"}} and status eq open.
